decision: After the crash, three evidence classes remain valid in descending strength, each with mandatory citation form: (1) LIVE_SCREEN_CONFIRMED claims — the pre-crash persisted boundary (timings.jsonl digest recorded before backfill, unmutated), the fresh recovery-session stable screenshot (sha256-bound), and crash-transcript message ranges with embedded browser observations — valid but citable ONLY as recovered/backfill evidence with the transcript digest and message ranges, never as original real-time raw trace; (2) SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_CONFIRMED claims — transcript-level only, cited by message identifiers with downgraded weight (no stable boundary was captured); (3) DERIVED claims — the recorded chain-link inference, citable only as inference together with its recorded basis. Operator-provided fresh visual evidence is valid for reconciliation but user_reported and explicitly excluded from autonomous detector validation. Anything requiring the original frames is invalid: WINGRUN_20260906_01 has zero durable frames, so per-week frame identifiers and wall-clock timestamps for recovered weeks do not exist, must never be fabricated, and retrieval must exclude or downgrade such rows.
facts: crash_recovery_backfill.json is explicitly labeled 'THIS IS RECOVERED SESSION EVIDENCE, NOT ORIGINAL REAL-TIME RAW TRACE' with recovery_class UNREGISTERED_RUN_CONTINUATION; it binds the crash-session transcript by sha256, the fresh recovery-session screenshot by sha256, and records the original timings.jsonl digest before backfill with mutated_by_recovery: false.

The backfill's own evidence tally is 12 LIVE_SCREEN_CONFIRMED events, 1 SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_CONFIRMED event (S2-to-S3 transition in progress at crash, 'no stable S3 HOME boundary was captured by the crash session'), and 1 DERIVED event (the chain-link inference, recorded with an explicit four-point basis); no event is classed UNKNOWN.

The backfill's recorded unknowns: original per-event wall-clock timestamps for recovered weeks were not durably persisted; original frame identifiers for recovered weeks were not durably persisted; the exact instant the S2-to-S3 transition became stable is absent from the crash session; cross-season fan-count semantics are not used as run-identity evidence.

The recorded diagnosis is PERSISTENCE_DURABILITY_FAILURE with game_state_mismatch false: the session continued live execution after the last durable timings write and crashed before persistence synchronized.

operator_reconcile_20260906_s3w1.json is provenance user_reported (operator-provided fresh visual evidence), explicitly 'NOT counted toward autonomous visual detector replication'; it records the incident of a screenshot tool hanging while the game transaction continued and committed the week, and lists as unknowns that the autonomous detector was not validated on that frame and that intermediate frames were not captured, with 'no fabricated frame IDs'.

artifact_registry.json carries WINGRUN_20260906_01 as COMPLETED_TARGET_NOT_MET, CLOSED, resume not allowed, with the backfill recorded as its recovery artifact, and the mainline runtime status for S1/S2 marked as recovered from crash-session evidence.

evidence_corpus_gap_report.md states WINGRUN_20260906_01 has 0 durable png (frames lost in the crash; the backfill cites non-durable session call ids) and that retrieval must either exclude or downgrade these rows; it also records that the registry (updated 2026-09-06) does not list the later 20260907 runs.

The gap report's must-not-autogenerate list marks process-side fields — run/trajectory linkage, authorization provenance, process-outcome category, and confidence for authorization decisions — as attachable only from durable records at ingest, never derived from pixels.
inferences: Citation discipline follows from the records: recovered events must carry the recovered-evidence notice, the transcript digest, and message-range citations; fresh boundaries must carry the sha256-bound screenshot; the persisted boundary keeps its pre-backfill digest; operator evidence must be marked user_reported; the chain-link continuity claim must be marked DERIVED with its basis — none of these may be presented as original real-time raw trace.

The reconstructed week-by-week history (S1W7 through S2W8, twelve LIVE_SCREEN_CONFIRMED events) is usable as recovered evidence anchored to transcript-embedded observations, but it is weaker than durably persisted originals precisely because timestamps and frame identifiers are absent.

Claims that would require the lost frames — per-week image evidence, intermediate frames between a lesson click and commit, or any fabricated frame identifier — are not reconstructible and must stay excluded, downgraded, or UNKNOWN.
unknowns: The exact instant the S2-to-S3 transition became stable is not present in the crash session; the chain-link claim that the fresh S3 boundary continues that transition remains DERIVED inference, not confirmed fact.
Original per-event wall-clock timestamps and original frame identifiers for all recovered weeks do not exist and are permanently unrecoverable from the records read.

The autonomous visual detector was not validated on the operator-reconciled frame, and intermediate frames of the committed week were never captured, so detector-level replication of that boundary is UNKNOWN.
The registry's currency is bounded: it does not reflect the 20260907 runs, so run-identity resolution for those corpora rests on directory and timing conventions rather than the registry.
reason: The records support a strict evidence-class answer: sha256-bound durable artifacts and transcript-anchored reconstructed events remain valid only when cited as recovered/backfill evidence with digests and message ranges; transcript-only claims stay transcript-level; the continuity claim stays DERIVED with its basis; operator visual evidence stays user_reported and outside detector validation; and everything dependent on the lost original frames — per-week frame identifiers, timestamps, intermediate frames — is UNKNOWN and must never be fabricated or silently upgraded, with retrieval excluding or downgrading those rows. This is an offline evidence-classification answer and grants no execution of any kind.
